brand: The Residual Stream · EP 06 · The block

lines.text: Vera, what's inside a transformer?
One block, stacked. GPT-2 small has 12; GPT-3 has 96.
lines.say: One block, stacked. G P T two small has twelve, G P T three has ninety-six.

lines.text: Like floors in a tall building.
What flows up through them?
Each token's vector, straight up: the residual stream.
Every part reads it, computes, and adds its result back. Nothing overwrites.
So it all just piles up.
Where do tokens talk to each other?
Only in attention. It moves information between positions.
So “her” can pull in “Mia”.
lines.say: So, her, can pull in, Mia.

lines.text: The only group chat in the building.
And the MLP?
Each token alone: expand about four times, a nonlinearity, project back.
lines.say: Each token alone: expand about four times, a non-linearity, project back.

lines.text: It holds roughly two thirds of a dense model's parameters.
Research suggests much factual recall happens there.
Why add? Why not replace?
Without residual connections, a signal through a hundred layers is distorted beyond recovery.
And gradients vanish on the way back.
Who figured that out?
Computer vision: ResNet, 2015.
Norms keep each sublayer's input at a stable scale.
lines.say: Norms keep each sub-layer's input at a stable scale.

lines.text: How big is a real one?
The guide's calculator says Llama 3 8B has 8.03 billion.
lines.say: The guide's calculator says Llama three, eight B, has eight point oh three billion.

lines.text: And the MLP's share?
lines.say: And the M L P's share?

lines.text: 70%. Real formulas, minus tiny norm and bias terms.
lines.say: Seventy percent. Real formulas, minus tiny norm and bias terms.

lines.text: Can I climb a block myself?
Step through it and try the calculator, in The block chapter.
One floor at a time. Adding, never erasing.
